object_description: solitary hall building with a staggered roof and a full-width street portico, plus a second social building
design_condition: the new hall follows the alignment of its predecessor and forms an ensemble with the school building, extending into the depths of the grounds to enclose the existing open space as a schoolyard

positive: The design is based on a careful analysis of the existing overall situation
The new hall follows the alignment of the previous one and forms a striking ensemble of public buildings
Moderate height development and tapering flanks subordinate it to the school building
This gives both the school building and the copper beech tree a strong presence
A portico covering the entire width lets the hall appear as a public building and forms the address to the street
Extending into the depths of the grounds encloses the existing open space with its plane trees as a schoolyard
The social building forms a courtyard-forming ensemble with the church centre and the restaurant
Materials and detailed solutions refer to the classicist school building, pointing to a dialogue between old and new
Portico, solid plinth and shingled gable fronts give structural use and show the richness of the design
Visible saddle roof girders span hall and stage with loads transferred to glulam facade supports
The interior conveys a friendly expression appropriate to the task
A staggered roof divides the cross-section into three areas of different heights
A band of windows at the roof offsets brings north light into the depth of the room
The hall faces south towards the playing field and receives light from two sides
The two-storey trapezoidal foyer opens to the forecourt in an inviting gesture
For larger events the vestibule can be opened to the hall and function as a filter and service zone
The gallery on the upper floor can be used as a spectator gallery, offering considerable added value
The basement with parking, toilets and storage is clearly laid out and well organised
The social building uses similar architectural elements and can be flexibly arranged on each long side
The two new buildings are cleverly placed in relation to each other through their staggered roofs
Closing the gap in the tree row and removing the central access gives the complex an address on the street
Natural stone paving forms a carpet emphasising the public nature of the site
The copper beech and a fountain form further meeting points
A new footpath integrates the social building well into the network of paths
Motorised access is completely concentrated at one corner
The buildings have a simple structure and can be expected to be cost-effective
The timber construction with a high degree of prefabrication is economical and sustainable
A very coherent response with good urban positioning and attractive outdoor spaces
The constructive design and atmospheric materialisation promise high architectural quality
negative: The opening to the forecourt is limited to the foyer glazing, so the building appears rather closed and introverted
The vestibule separates the equipment room from the two parts of the hall
There is no disabled access to the stage rooms
The colonnade design needs strengthening to be more representative and inviting
The natural stone carpet needs review for rainwater management and heat reduction
The tree population needs further development for space creation, shading and habitats
The kink in the side facades needs cleaning up in coordination with the monopitch roofs
The position for catering deliveries needs examination to separate people and vehicle flows
The stage should open more to the schoolyard for outdoor performances
The internal access, especially to the stage, needs enlarging
